claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in North Karelia wellbeing services county was 1.0% below the national level (ratio 0.99, 95% interval 0.954-1.028), about 4.3 fewer deaths a year than its age structure predicts.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: North Karelia wellbeing services county is at 66.43 (three-year mean to 2024) against 73.4 nationally and a target of 80.

Waiting time of over 3 months since assessment of the need for treatment for a non-emergency appointment with a primary health care doctor in outpatient care, % of completed appointments: North Karelia wellbeing services county is at 3.47 (three-year mean to 2025) against 1.7 nationally.

Referrals for specialised health care received after processing for more than 21 days, % of the referrals received: North Karelia wellbeing services county is at 2.33 (three-year mean to 2025) against 1 nationally.

Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants: North Karelia wellbeing services county is at 79.3 (three-year mean to 2025) against 36 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where North Karelia wellbeing services county is clearly worse than the country is early detection (screening participation).

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 7.8 deaths a year in North Karelia wellbeing services county (range 1.2-15.6) for an assumed EUR 242,127 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 92% of sensitivity runs.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 66.4% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 22% of the gap.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 75.9% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-4.07 percentage points, closing about 74% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
